This is one of these sad situations in which you wanted to love a game, but it makes an effort to annoy you.
Beyond Sol is a mix between Top-Down Space Sims and 4X, a rather rare (and amazing mix), in a lightweight implementation.
The game has a solid foundation, and is probably the fastest Space-Sim-with-4X-component to learn and start playing.
Combat is straightforward, there's a decent amount of upgrades that can let you tailor your ship to your needs or playstyle, there's varying amounts of activity: random events that can include resource-rich comets, bounty hunting missions, responding to distress signals or joining an on-going battle.
There's no bugs or apparent lack of polish.
4X elements involve building 'fleets', diplomacy, trading and war.
For a space game (which are usually niche, therefore clunky and convoluted), Beyond Sol has a remarkably simple and functional building system: you snap things where they fit, and you're done. You build Military Bases/Mining Bases/Radar Stations in the middle of a sector (a hex, on the map) and you're done.
This makes it so you're always on the move, always doing something worthwhile, which is usually not the case in a large part of space games.
Most importantly: killing enemies, building well, and overall learning to play with the best strategies feel satisfying - which is the most important thing for this sort of game.
Praise must also be given to the fact that this was made by a small team (one person, as far as I know), in a short budget and time. This is amazing in an age of eternal Early Access of 20+ man teams with funding beyond necessary.
And the game also has
, which is such a rare thing for this type of game!
All of this makes it frustrating and sad not to recommend the game.
All the goodness mentioned above makes the first couple hours of the game feel great if you're into Space Sims and Top-Down Shooters. However, as you advance a bit into the game, it immediately falls flat, as everything is the game feels like a chore in order to grind money for upgrades and City Building.
Trading is 100% hit-and-miss: there's no indication of prices (directly tied to supply/demand) other than extremely rare "surplus" or "lacking" events. As trading is the fastest way to make money, the game becomes a
in which you fly around in a convoy, buying low and selling high with no idea of where to buy, where to sell, and why prices and stock are the way they are. Empires that don't produce Titanium will, for some reason, have random a surplus of Titanium.

Wars are fought in similar fashion to Grand Strategy games, in which the more damage you inflict, the more "Warscore" you get. Higher war score = higher war reparations (losing side pays you for peace), which is usually not even enough to pay for your [constant] losses.
If you don't accept the enemy peace treaty after you did some damage (killed 2-3 buildings or stations), you are punished by making every other faction in the world hate you for being a warmonger. This can result in an instant mess / loss of the game if you're not aware of that.
If you do accept the Peace Treaty, you have to wait 20 minutes before declaring war to that faction again. And they probably will declare war on you once the 20 minutes are over, because now they hate you.
It makes the whole construction of a fleet, upgrading your ship, and building your empire feel worthless.
Sending gifts, trading eventually with a faction, flying around and helping in battes and distress calls is the only way to raise diplomacy. This feels cool in the beggining, but when you are fighting 2 wars, dealing with pirate bases, trying to make enough money to scare off invaders..it becomes hard to find time to personally go help another faction. It feels weird having an empire and fleets that won't help on-demand.
Although the game shouldn't be bashed for this (due to scope, funding and time commitments), it feels weird that you are the only 'real' ship doing stuff in the world. Everything else, other than the static AI fleets that mostly react to in-game events, is random and has no inherent meaning. An example of this is when you respond a distress call and you find that the Freighter under attack is from YOUR faction. Who is that trader? Where did it come from? Where it is going?
A living, simulated world is not an easy task to tackle, but I believe the issue must be mentioned. The more you play, the more awkward and repetitive it feels.
Similar to the point above, AI factions will grow with no explanation of where they acquired their money or resources. Factions with 5 resource spots might grow as fast as factions with 0-1 resource spots, making the game feel shallow and just plain wrong.
Do note that none of these issues - that outright kill the fun, depending on your expectations - were caused by lack of funding or development time (except for things that involve more simulation). The way Trading and Warfare is handled, for instance, were awkward design decisions that feel like are in place to artificially prolong games.
An example situation is that destroying one of 10 AI empires (a common goal) will take forever and is just not worth the money for the time.
As I mentioned, I'd love to simply recommend this game. Space games are my main thing, and I throw money at developers of the genre whenever I'm able. I write reviews for the genre whenever I'm able. The reason for that is because I want to see the genre evolve, as it's very niche.
Beyond Sol is not a situation in which I hate the game, it's a situation in which I feel sad as just a few tweaks could have made the game much more solid, and very fun. It could've been an indie gem of the genre.
If players were able to mod the game, an insane amount of content and changes could be made. To me, it feels even worse that the developer simply moved on - I seriously hope the concept is either revisited, or the lessons learned are implemented on his new project -
.

My suggestion is to check out
. Although there's a difference in scope, it's a similar game without the cons listed above.

Многие игроки ждали эту игру с нетерпением, так как ее дату выхода неоднократно переносили. Вот она вышла и я тоже не исключение поиграл в нее и от игры остались неплохие впечатления. Конечно же у игры есть свои минусы, но плюсов намного больше. Игра "GTA 5" была разработана студией "Rockstar North", а выпущена "Rockstar Games" и поразила не мало игроков.
О игре рассказывать можно очень много, так как она разнообразная. Сюжет у игры очень интересный и развивается по ходу игры, рассказывать о нем нет смысла, так как играть потом будет не так интересно.
Игра представляет собой открытый мир, в котором делать можно все что пожелаете. В управление игроку дается три персонажа, за каждого из которых можно играть и выбирать в любой момент игры, не считая миссий. По ходу прохождения игры в некоторых миссиях нужно будет играть различными персонажами, что очень интересно. Например взяли вашего напарника в плен, переключились на другого персонажа и легко спасли его. Очень интересно сделали то, что когда переключаешь на другого персонажа, он не стоит там где вы закончили играть с ним в последний раз, а занимается свои каким нибудь делом.
У каждого персонажа будут свои определенные миссии, которые вы не сможете пройти другим персонажем. Также будут доступны дополнительные миссии, которые также очень интересно проходить. По мимо всех миссий в игре, можно развивать каждого персонажа, например бегать, стрелять в тире и многое многое другое. Заняться в игре по мимо основных миссий есть чем.
Очень понравился вид от первого лица, в перестрелках можно переключаться и получится как будто играешь в шутер. Там уже на любителя.
Графика в игре очень красивая и приятная, мне понравилась. Присутствует смена дня и ночи, очень красочно смотрится закат.
Теперь расскажу немного о минусах игры, которые мне не понравились. Когда ездишь на машинах как бы думаешь что можно сносить все подряд, но нет бывают попадаются столбы которые без проблем сносишь, а есть маленькие столбики, которые невозможно снести. Вот эти моменты не очень понравились, так как иногда в погонях, некоторые предметы, которые думаешь снесутся без проблем, наоборот тормозят тебя.
Также очень неудобно это конечно же что нет русской озвучки, без нее очень тяжеловато, потому что в основном смотришь только ролики, а так когда идет бой или едешь на задании читать просто не успеваешь. Пытался пару раз читать, но часто врубаешься и вообще получается неразбериха.
Несмотря на эти мелкие минусы мне игра сильно понравилась, очень веселая, задорная и сильно затягивает своим сюжетом. Рекомендую ознакомиться так как игра достойна своего внимания.

Type of Game:
Procedural Death Labyrinth (PDL) First Person Shooter (FPS ) or FPSPDL
Version Played:
PC version through Steam
Similar Games:
Paranautical Activity, Tower of Guns, HeXen, and to a lesser degree The Binding of Isaac
The Good:
FPS gameplay that is frantic and twitch-based, which brings back a feeling of playing old school Quake or an even better comparison Hexen
Four different weapon categories, which feature different ammo types for each. All weapons are projectile-based, but some feature area of effect damage or spread functionality. Weapons are varied enough to keep things interesting.
Numerous procedurally generated rooms that offer a strong challenge in the sense of number of enemies or traps to avoid
Progression is rewarded with abilities that make give the player mild advantages.
For example: Health will restore slightly when entering a new combat room. This is a great ability as health potion drops are very infrequent
There are also permanent progression unlocks in the form of new characters, which feature different starting abilities
All of these choices drastically impact your play through and add a wonderful level of strategy to the gameplay
The game is challenging in a way that requires you to constantly be aware of your surroundings. You can quickly find yourself cornered or stuck on a pillar, which could equal your demise. I found the difficulty suspenseful and rewarding, which are the reasons I enjoy PDLs so much.
The art style is Gothic, which lends to the overall archaic design of the maps. You feel as though magic is a common companion to this game world, which appears to be the subject matter
There are many different enemy types and some creative ones as well (I’m looking at you weird floating whale creature), which all have different battle tactics. Facing a new enemy is both fascinating and frustrating.
There are also boss battles, which offer variations of other enemy-types you’ve faced off against. They are large and difficult to overcome, which again adds to the satisfaction when you beat them.
The Bad:
The game has an ending, but doesn’t offer much in the way of end-game content after you do so. There is no New Game+ or added bosses (think Binding of Isaac). Once you’ve beaten the game there is little motivation to return to it. A successful run can take as short as a couple hours, which is disappointing considering how much content this game features
Puzzle sections feature FPS platforming, which I feel is always a difficult mechanic to pull off. Since you can’t see your feet, timing your jumps with the location of your player’s body is tedious and unnecessarily frustrating.
Gameplay itself can get stale, as once you’ve seen all the weapons there is little variation to the strategy. Dash around and shoot at all the enemies then jump around a frustrating platforming puzzle then repeat.
Can you play it while the children are awake?
The monsters are creepy and well designed and as I mentioned above there is a strong Gothic influence, which can create a scary atmosphere. I would say it is fine for older children, but the younger ones may let their imagination run wild and be scared of the content.
Did I make time to complete it?
Yes. It took me a few hours to run through the entire game. Unfortunately, there was little incentive for me to return.
Recommended Purchase Price:
Ziggurat is an easy sell for someone who is both a fan of First Person Shooters and Procedural Death Labyrinths, there is much here to like. Whether it is the well crafted progression system, enemy type variation, random room generation, fast and crazy projectile combat, or the enjoyment of defeating a particularly difficult boss you’ll find something to enjoy! The only caveat to this would be the replayability of Ziggurat, as once you’ve completed the game there is little reason to return. I recommend a purchase price of $12.99.

I checked this game out after I looked for something similar to Paranautical Activity and I was pretty happy I found Zigguratt.
I really enjoyed my time with the game. It's fun, challenging and looks pretty great. A successful run takes around an hour or so, not too long, not too short (although that's just my personal taste).
Boss fights are pretty challenging, even if i havent encountered too many different bosses.
You start with one unlocked Character and by fulfilling certain criteria (like killing 200 Carrots, Beating the game once, etc.) you'll unlock new characters with different starting abilities and new items.
However, my biggest disappointment with the game is the lack of powerful upgrades/items. Theres a decent amount of Level-Ups you'll get in a run, each level-up giving you a choice of one of two Upgrades. At the start of every Floor (5 in total) you get a new kind of Spell (there are 3 kinds of "spells", Alchemy (basically bombs), Staves and Spells). Sometimes you'll stumble across Amulets that are activatable items with a recharge timer. Now, it might be because I haven't unlocked a ton of stuff, but I've found myself getting the same upgrades again and again.
Coming from Paranautical Activity and other rogue-lites (like Binding of Isaac) I was used to the mechanic of Item Rooms/Shops on every floor and an upgrade after every Boss. I kinda missed that in Ziggurat and in turn I'm missing some of the replay value of say BoI, where every run can turn out completely different. But that's just my personal preference.
In case you care about a Rogue-lite's story: Ziggurat's story is fairly simple but pretty cool and interesting (I really liked the cutscenes, the artstyle is just lovely):
You're a Wizard Apprentice taking part in a Test to become part of the most powerful group of Wizards, but I thought the ending was pretty disappointing if I'm honest.
tl;dr:
Wouldn't pick it up fullprice, but at a 33%-50% discount it's definitely worth the money :)

CONS: It is free-to-play BUT it is very much structured to make playing without buying TPs (Turbine Points) as annoying as possible.  For a start, there is the 2 gold pieces money cap - you need TPs to remove that.  And you can hit 2GP in an hour's play.  Yes, you can eran TPs but it's sloooooow.  And fellowships (forming a party) is a pain and you really need to make sure your fellow fellows know what they are doing.  I got to level 23 without dying, joined a fellowship for a dungeon and died almost immediately.  The housing system can leave you miles from where the action is so you'll probably end up buying and selling several homes.

This game is best described as a humorous cross between a clicker/idle game and a dating sim. Click your way to a girl's heart with romantic dates, fancy gifts, awkward conversation and excessive poking. Manage up to sixteen different careers to buy her that cute puppy and still have enough free time for your dozen hobbies. Then find yourself waiting impatiently for all those colorful progress bars to fill up.
Crush Crush is a light-hearted indie game that pokes fun at contemporary gaming, cartoons, and movies. The game mechanics are easy to learn and allow for both active and passive playstyles. The art is quite good for an indie and the music/sounds are acceptable. The writing is appropriately flirty, with no lack of bad pick-up lines, uncomfortable innuendo and the occasional touching moment. Overall, I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a funny casual game with a hint of resource management and romance.

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons
This game is entirely unique compared to many other mediums of not only video games, but storytelling of media in general. The soundtrack fits with the story, the story fits with the characters, the characters fit with the environment, the environment fits with the controls, and it all adds up to a crowning achievement in indie video game history.
While short (only 2-3 hours) when looked at as solely a game, look at it more as a way for video games to fully showcase its potential to deliver lush, beautiful, and captivating story, intertwined with a unique control scheme and an interesting, yet deceptive world. Most films do not achieve this for the price. You will replay this not for the extra features, nor the countless hours of customizable gameplay or differing endings. You will play this because it sets the bar for video games to not only challenge cinema as a storytelling medium, but to exceed its capabilities and unlock the potential for games in the future to follow suit.
This title isn't for everyone. However, for people who like serious stories, mystic music, perfectly woven in gameplay, and an artistic journey through a land of mysterious yet intriguing characters, this title is a must-have.

I was blown away by Human Revolution and poured far too many hours into it (on a non-Steam version) than is healthy. I was a bit wary of this latest outing bearing in mind the user reviews it's got but thankfully I found Mankind Divided to be every bit as much fun as its predecessor. It really doesn't deserve the shitcanning it's received.
It has all the deep, rich gameplay options we've come to expect from Deus Ex and adds some fun new augs too. I had a lot of fun with Remote Hacking and Icarus Dash. Being able to craft your own biocells and multitools also gives you a lot more freedom.
Not being a big fan of boss battles, I was glad that there was only one and that it's possible to finish it in a variety of ways, both lethal and non-lethal.
Although the quality of the graphics is way ahead of HR, it doesn't quite have the same level of visual panache. The neo-renaissance stylings have given way to a more sombre aesthetic that nonetheless still gets the job done. The music, however, is every bit as lush and gorgeous as that of Human Resistance.
There is more than enough here in terms of missions, both main and side, to keep you busy for a good while though. I've just finished my first run and clocked up 55 hours doing it, though I'm one of those people who likes to crawl into every  vent and hack every computer I can find. Pretty sure I missed a few though. If you pay attention you might discover a surprise cameo from Farida Malik...
If you like Deus Ex: Human Revolution, chances are you'll also enjoy Mankind Divided.

GTA is in itself, especially story-wise, a great game with loads of features and tons of stuff to do.
Multiplayer is an extension of that and what I will be focusing on here.
It brings a bunch of new vehicles, features, missions, characters into the game and allows you to play, with friends or alone, in the city of Los Santos and do as you wish. Fly a bomber plane, get a tank, buy an office and start stealing cars, buy a yacht.
Multiplayer does however also include outragiously priced items such as a 50000 hat or a 100000 Suit. And that is just the clothing - which is optional. Vehicle prices skyrocket from "acceptable, but high" to "insane" very, very quickly. Some "normal" super cars cost upwards of 2 million dollars, with more added rather frequently. Others, so called "special vehicles" cost upwards of 3 million - the APC for example.
There are a bunch of buisnesses for the player to run, you can craft weapons and sell them, smuggle narcotics and other illegal stuff, become a CEO and steal cars/supply crates or get yourself a motorcycle club and produce drugs which you then sell.
Those are some amazing things to do, admittedly. The issue, with all of them consnsitently, is the pricing. 4 million dollars for an office, between 1 and 3 million for a bunker, another 2 to 3 for a hangar - the motorcycle club actually comes in rather cheap at 200000 dollars. Oh, I nearly forgot, to actually make money you again have to invest into your buisness, sometimes going over one million dollars.
Now lets get into the cool stuff, I will just list a few prices here:
With the, at the writing of this review, most recent DLC airplanes were added into the game. Most of these are really rather cool to fly and kill people with - but at the same time the cool ones start 4-5 000 000 $.
With the update before that the developers added a sniper rifle that shoots explosive rounds. It takes just a few of those shots to, without exception, destroy all airplanes. Heck you don't even need to reload to get multiple of them.
Now the prices wouldn't be that bad if it weren't for the fact that you have to grind for ages to get anything done. Hours to get to 500k, and guess what, you need 10 times that. Easily.
Rockstar has also decided to drip-feed content to the users over weeks, even months, which makes it even worse. New content would be great if it would be affordable.

For a game essentially developped by one programmer over one year, this is excellent little gem. It's a shame it didn't sell as well allowing for further development and content. It still however makes a great blend of two genres, namely 4x type strategy (real-time) and space action. You control a ship (which you can equip and swap for another ship) flying around the solar system trying to get your orbital city to dominate other such cities present in the system. You aim to dominate your solar system either through a diplomatic, economic or militaristic victory. Only then will Earth (Sol) name you the leader of said system.
There are constant events or mini-missions around you which keep you busy, as well as the occasional pirate encounter which is fun, because the combat is exciting and has depth depending on how you are equipped and which ships you add to your fleet. The game plays similar to League of Legends rather than a traditional top-down WASD, but this works in its favour.
Definitely a great experience when playing multiplayer (Port-forwarding necessary), and all in all a positive experience. Hopefully they come out with a sequel or some sort of expansion.

This game is an interesting animal in that it is an RTS cunningly disguised as a 4X.
You start with a single city, and as far as I've found a single city is all you get. You can build things like housing, power and manufacturing which attach to your central city node, and those buildings will allow you to build more stuff or upgrade your older buildings. As you expand, the fleet that accompanies the player-craft can be expanded (and military bases can also have fleets) and then you use those fleets to further expand the empire.
Visually, the game is ok, audio is nice and the soundtrack is effective, no concerns about the media. However, I DO have concerns about the depth, if you are trying to write an RTS that appeals to the 4X crowd, well, we like our content, and there isn't really enough at the moment.
By trying to be at once an RTS and a 4X, it's managed to lose the strategy of the RTS, and without some of the depth of a 4X to compensate, I'm really struggling to decide whether to recommend this game or not.
I think, for now, It's going to have to be 'not', however, I will more than happily change that to the opposite if the situation changes, I actually want to recommend it, so giving me an excuse to do so would be awesome.

First of all - I've spent countless hours in this game before I finally downloaded it through steam when I had to re-install it due to hardware problems.
The Lord of the Rings Online boasts a great open world based on J.R.R. Tolkien's famous works. Here you get to explore Middle-earth at your own pace, together with friends or all alone. Since LOTRO was first launched in 2007, it has grown from being a fairly small MMO to be among the biggest and broadest worlds out there. You can explore famous sites as seen in the movies and read about in the books, such as the Shire, Bree-town, Weathertop, Rivendell, Isengard, Helms Deep and as of one of the more recent updates, Minas Tirith! And not only do you get to see these landmarks, but you can also explore everything inbetween.
Okay, you can't go everywhere straight off. In fact there is alot you'll have to go through to get to Gondor and Minas Tirith, but the story and places you visit on your way is just so masterfully created. You create your own character and you get to be the hero of Middle-earth in your own adventure paralell to the travels of Frodo and the fellowship. You'll see sides of Middle-earth that you never really noticed in either the books or films before.
And the best thing about LOTRO is that it is completely free to play! Okay, you can buy Turbine Points and VIP membership to help you on your adventures. But it is also completely possible to farm Turbine Points in-game and get to the level cap, which is currently at level 105, without spending a single real-life dollar.
I recommend this game to anyone who has a slight interest in Tolkien's work, be it the books or the movies based on them. I also recommend it to anyone who likes a good MMORPG and wants to try something a little different. Because LOTRO is different from other MMO's. Not only does it have by far the most established lore of any MMO, but it also has one of the very best player communities. Sure, there are a few jerks in Middle-earth too, just as there are in any other place, but overall the LOTRO community is among the friendliest and most helpful communities out there.
The only con I can state about this game right now is that since it's come so far in development it is a little hard for new players and those of us, me included, who's taken a longer break from the game, to catch up with the newest content. But luckily, the friendly community has got you covered! If you ask for help, I bet you're gonna get it!

This has been on my wishlist for a while but I couldn't bring myself to pay 15 bucks for a game described as "short". Patience paid off and I purchased it for  $1.50.
It's definitly a quality game with some unique facets. The brothers  aren't on some super-complicated quest, so the story is short. However, shorter is better in this case--any longer and the puzzle solving mechanics would've gotten stale.
For me the highlight of the game was the contoller aspect. Playing/controlling both of the brothers at the same time is counterintuitive, both mechanically and mentally. The controls are emmeshed with the storyline and while the mechanics can be frustrating, it makes for a more challenging experience. You literally can't make any progress without the other brother and that, more than anything fleshes out the game and the characters. When the player gets closer to the end of the story, they'll see that those controls are for more than just moving the brothers around. If anything tugged at my heart strings, it was the change in controller usage by the end.
Speaking of tugging heartstrings...
Other players have described this game as being a "tear-jerker". If it were longer and if the characters were more fleshed out, I would agree.  That's not to say the story doesn't have a lot of heart and meaning, it does, it's just not as sad as say,  The Walking Dead or Life is Strange (or those super stress inducing games like Beholder and This War of Mine--I know, totally different set-ups but they're crazy depressing). A lack of tears (in my experience) isn't negative though. The brothers connected with me as much as I expected. They were funny at times and you can see a bond between them but their goal is so time-sensitive that they don't have a lot of time to develop. Plus, they speak in something very similiar to Sim-lish.
So in short, saddish but not to the point of tears.
Also,the game's atmosphere is beautiful. Lot's of breathaking effects and design elements.  I wasn't 100% on board with the music but it doesn't take much away from the gameplay.
For a short game, it's fun, meaningful and unique. It's definitely worth a play through but I'd watch for a sale. Fifteen dollars is a little much for how much playing time you get.

First and foremost, Brothers is a story. It's right there in the title: a tale of two sons.
It's a game, yes, in that you direct the protagonists along a path and interact with the world around them, but there's no level grinding or speed runs or twitch shooting. It's more of an interactive adventure, in the vein of ICO or Journey, that requires your contribution to make you an active participant in the events to come.
Your mission is to get the brothers from point A to point B, and marvel at the scenery as their journey unfolds before you. It's at times breathtaking, at times terrifying, and at times heartwrenching, but always overflowing with a level of creative originality and imagination I've rarely seen in any media. It's beautiful, but be forewarned: Not everything beautiful is necessarily pretty.
As befitting a chiefly narrative title, gameplay is fairly easy and forgiving. The mechanics involved are all just a means to an end, a way to get you to the next page. It requires a dual-analog gamepad to play, but I don't think it could have been made any other way. I used a wireless 360 controller and had no problems. The only real challenges are the mildly ambidextrous requirement of controlling two characters at the same time (which thankfully never becomes excessively complicated) and the occasionally unclear path traversal where you die a few times trying to figure out exactly what it was they intended for you to do. Usually the pathing and direction are clear, but certain rare interactions were only used once and never adequately introduced. So maybe you have to retry a few times before you get it right, but then it IS a game, after all. Though the story is so powerful you could be forgiven for forgetting that fact at times.

The game itself was fun and is worth picking up on a Winter/Summer sale or something if it's like $15-20 but the problem is the game just ends too soon. There is one "boss" who if you go for the achievement (Killswitch) you don't even get to fight which was pretty disappointing. Other than that its a typical Deus Ex game but it just feels unfinished and to have a game that ships as what I would consider unfinished have day1 DLC is a shame.
It took me ~24 hours to beat the game and I collected just about everything I could, primarily did missions as stealth (which takes significantly longer typically), and did most (if not all) of the side missions.

I thought the game was excellent however the ending has been very unpopular. I feel this may be due to the final boss feeling like a minor character, which is emphasised by the final cinematic pointing out the "real" villains, cheapening your accomplishments. But at the end of the day I really enjoyed it. the gameplay improved on Human Revolution in many ways, and my played time was about 30 hours, the same as my played time in both the original Deus Ex and Human Revolution. So in reality you get pretty much the same amount of content, but it's just the story that leaves you unsatisfied.
I still recommend the game as I had a ton of fun completing it, and there are a lot of fun side missions to do.
On a side note, if you are waiting for the Deus Ex game that has a booming nightclub that sounds like its heaving from the outside, only for there to be like 4 patrons when you enter, this is not the Deus Ex game for you.

Story: 7/10
I think the story was fine for what it is. There was a lot of sibling stuff that made it seem a little awkward at times and the rhyming scheme was a little corny but it made it entertaining. It was kind of a generic story where one sibling defects and the other good sibling ends up saving them yada yada etc etc nothing too creative but it wasn’t bad at all. The story didn’t turn me off to the game by any means.
Graphics: 10/10
I personally absolutely love the side scrolling style of this game. I also played the game on PS4 with a 3D tv, and I’d say that playing it on steam is just as breathtaking. The colors, and environment are all really beautiful and well designed, placed with purpose and very visually appealing. I think that the use of the environment within the game is also brilliant too. Everything is very crisp and just real pretty.
Audio: 10/10
I love the soundtrack, A LOT. The game has a very alluring style and I could listen to it constantly. The voiceovers aren’t too bad either, but they can get a little alloying after a while. However, you are given the option to adjust audio options and that works for me after I’ve heard enough. PLUS, I think some of the puns and stuff that are used are really silly and they make me laugh, so I do like them.
Gameplay: 9/10
Best with a friend. I have the most fun when playing this game when I’m playing with a friend, because the combat is just more entertaining and the puzzles become more of a partnership in figuring them out. Also the game allows numerous opportunities to show off, and I really like that too. I gave it a 9 because it glitches out sometimes, but it's nothing that would stop me from playing.
Replay Value: 10/10
There is lots to do after you beat the game! Like go back and collect experience,  paintings to collect (which unlock a bonus level), get through the game on hardcore/hard, and lots of other achievements. I would honestly keep replaying this game even if I completed all the achievements just because it’s fun to play, especially with other people.
Buy? 10/10
Definitely buy it. Make sure to buy the complete story so you can experience all the fun stuff from start to finish. You won’t regret it because it’s an absolutely gorgeous game and it’s a lot of fun in general.

This is a fantastic game. I am not a fan of rogue-lites (like Binding of Issac) because the combat mechanics tend to be an afterthought in comparison to the design of randomly generated items and rooms. The developers of Ziggurat clearly focused on gameplay in equal measure to every other aspect of the game design, which makes this the most fun and exciting rogue-lite I have ever played. The FPS design feels like shooters from the late 90s and early 2000s that favoured unrealistic but interesting mechanics. The upgrades are card based and remind me of the system from Dragon's Crown. A great game that rogue-lite and non rogue-lite fans will both enjoy.

I was very hopeful for this game when i first saw it pop up on steam. I waited a little bit to get it at first because I was worried it was going to be another stinker, but man was I pleasantly surprised.
The game uses a randomly generated dungeon that you crawl through in FPS style blasting your way through rooms of enemies using wands, spells, staves, and alchemy. The combat is fast paced, graphically pleasing, and entertaining everytime you pick up and play. You basically work your way from room to room attempting to find a key that allows you to fight a boss to progress to the next floor. As you go, you level up and collect new weapons/items to help you along the way. Death is permanent, so if you die your back to zero. This is a good thing though, as it keeps the game from getting stale or feeling grindy. There is just enough punishment in death to make you feel like you messed up, but not punish you so much you feel like you won't get back to where you were.  You just start a new game and you will be leveling up and slaying baddies again within minutes.
Enemy types are varied and each one brings a different attack strategy and strengths/weaknesses to the table. You will have to constantly be aware of your surroundings and the type of enemies you are being attacked by to survive, always adapting your tactics to what abilities you have in your arsenal and what types of monsters spawned in the room.
One of the things I love most about this game is that you can pick it up and play for 15 minutes, or sit down and play for 2-3 hours and have a great experience either way. You are allowed to save in between floors and the early levels won't take much longer than 10-15 minutes so it works perfectly.
I feel like this game will only get better from here as the devs have already patched this game several times in the short week that I have owned it. They are fantastic and deserve all the credit they have gotten for this game and so very much more! Do them and yourself a favor by picking up this game and reccomending it to everyone you know!
EDIT: upate as of 10/17/15 this game just gets better and better. Every update is lovingly crafted by the devs and adds new rooms, perks, weapons, and enemies. I CANNOT reccomend this game ENOUGH. It is a blast and has easily found itself on the list of my favorite games of all time. I am very close to 100% completing and I have enjoyed every minute of it! THANK YOU DEVELOPERS FOR SUCH A WONDERFUL EXPERIENCE!
EDIT 2: Took almost 50 hours and I finally 100% completed this game. Worth every second spent. I loved this experience. Can't wait to see what game the devs have in store next.

Overview:
- Fast-paced FPS action.
- Pleasant graphical style that runs smoothly.
- Good variety in rooms, monsters, weapons and powers-ups.
- A responsible Developer that has updated the game, and added content, several times since release.
Ziggurat has instantly become my favorite game of the year. I've been looking for a Rogue-lite to capture my attention and entertain me and now I'm absorbed.
Game Features:
- Numerous different unlockable Mages to to play. Each Mage has unique starting attributes and unique firing types for the different weapons in he game.
- Four different types of weapons (Wand, Spells, Staff, Alchemy) with each weapon type also having different sub-types which not only do different types of damage but also deliver the damage in a unique way.
- Multiple different rooms of type, sizes and design. Rooms with large horizontal space, vertical space, mazes, lots of nooks, traps, hazards, etc ...
- Interesting progression options and power-ups in the form of Amulets and Shrines.
So far I have enjoyed every minute spent in the game.

My wife is barren, and my seed is weak.  Alas, we remain a childless couple.  The fates would have us living in a near empty household, if not for the generosity of a dear friend. Upon returning to my manse, I was delighted to hear sounds of children coming from my study.  Were they my nieces and nephews? The cries of babes dashed that thought, for the offspring of my brothers and sisters are but a few years shy of adulthood. I ventured into my favourite room to find my wife at the computer.  "Diaper Dash!" she exclaimed happily.  Seeing my quizzical expression, she continued: "One of your Steam friends gifted it to you - thinking it would make a good prank." Laughing, I hugged my wife - both happy for her enthusiasm and the sounds of children in the house, digital though they might be.  "You may be barren," said I, "but no longer is our house barren of the simple and modest joys of infants."
I then pulled up a chair and joined my wife in a 5-minute session of Diaper Dash. As one who is used to indepth strategy, I easily worked out how to play the game.  Nor being no stranger to the demands of modern gaming I had no concerns with the level of multitasking required.  Whilst the graphics are childish, music uninspired, and a lack of complexity in the gameplay, it more than makes up for the eternally sad fact that my partner and I are unable to have children.  Hence, if your wife is barren, you can do no less a greater thing than to purchase Diaper Dash.  Some would love their offspring to remain eternally youthful; I can assure, good sirs and madams, that this game (as expected, given the title) only deals with infants - and the tribulations associated with them.
However, if you indeed have children, or are expecting a child, I urge you to play the game, for to abstain would also remove you of the chance to become better at managing infants.  In fact, I would hazard the opinion that maternity centres and colleges are less capable of educating you as a parent than this esteemed game.

Well it's one of those free games that kept me around for 50+ hours. Still have it installed. It's gotta be good.
For the sake of brevity I'll just use pros and cons to express my thoughts here.
PROS:
Multiplayer and a lot of it. 2v2, 1v1, free-for-all, and probably more. I'm just in it for the 2v2 and boy oh boy is it everything I wanted. Grab a friend, choose your characters, and then get paired up with two other people and duke it out.
Easy to find people online, the community is alive and well. (December 2016)
Lots of content. More characters and weapons then I know what to do with. It's psuedo content in truth because the game is based on fighting archetypes rather than unique characters, Hammer slow, gun fast, lance slow, sword fast, et cetera. That's not to say that you'll feel like you've hit the end of the content immediately, but there are trends.
You can throw your weapons and it adds a lot of variety to the game. Some spam weapon throws, some strategise.
Very fluid gameplay. Spikes, techs, and double jumps all make Smash Bros. players feel at home early on. It does lack a few key elements of Smash that I liked, but this game does well to follow suit in terms of fast-paced combat.
Still being updated. Always a big plus. Took a break for a few months and came back to a handful of new characters.
CONS:
The networking is good, but unfortunately falls short of what's necessary to accomodate for a fast-paced fighting game like this. Against the right opponent you'll have a smooth match with little hiccup and everything will feel right. Against an opponent on wi-fi or from across the country, air dodges turn into vanishing acts and i-frames exponentially increase as you play catch up and aggressively try to get a single hit in on somebody who's doing little more than just jump around in random directions. It can be a real headache dealing with these opponents, but that's the risk you take playing against random players online. Get the right opponents and the netcode is fine. Even at its worst, still better than Skullgirl's netcode.
The matchmaking is awful. I can go from winning 20 matches in a row, to playing against a player of equal skill, then go immediately back to a player that falls off the cliff 5 seconds into the match attempting to grab a weapon off the ground. There doesn't appear to be any sort of matchmaking algorithm and it makes playing online very frustrating. I'm more than willing to get my♥♥♥♥♥kicked, but if I get paired up with people who haven't earned their rank and I get comfortable with that skill level, then it makes it so I never get better. There's zero progression climb. 59 hours in and every match is entirely different.
The grind for the in-game currency is.. fair, but only if you're sticking to one or two characters. I've acquired less than 100k coins in the 50+ hours I've played the game and just to get White/Black skins for your character will set you back 10k/25k respectively. (Or at least I think that's what it was. Either way, it was certaintly a hit to the wallet.) That said, at least there's quite a bit of content that's buyable with the in-game currency. I'm not a big fan of most of the premium skins anyway.
Final thoughts:
Would love to see a clean-up of the matchmaking alogorithm (if there even is one in ranked), but otherwise the game is one of the best fighting games out there and it's free. If you don't mind the aesthetics of the game, give it a try.

Taken on its own, Deus Ex: Mankind Divided is a decent game; a large, interesting, semi-open world to explore, a branching storyline with multiple ways to progress through it. It's visually very nice and there's certainly plenty to do.
However, when compared to its predecessor, Deus Ex: Human Revolution (which is not without its own problems), this feels small, hollow and very much 'more of the same'. While it does fix many of DX:HR's problems, it introduces some of its own; but the main issue I found was an overarching lack of interest. I found myself getting bored as I progressed through the storyline. I'm now fairly close to the end with little desire to endure the painfully long loading times to finish.
It is definitely recommended, especially if you own a PC that's likely to speed up the load times (I've found it excruciatingly slow on my medium-spec PC), and if you either have more patience than me or haven't played the prequel, it's even more highly recommended. Just don't expect a masterpiece.

Mankind Divided can be summed up as an excellent improvment and sequel to Human Revolution. If you liked HR, you'll more certainly like this game. Otherwise, you most certainly won't like it.
Downsides are: the story remains weak on some aspects, there's FAR too much a focus on augs and you might encounter a few occasional bugs / gameplay issues.
However, the gameplay is great. The level design is incredibly beautiful, especially in Prague, although the amount of details can be confusing. The story-telling and atmosphere is even greater and more compelling than in Human Revolution.
The story has some weaknesses: how can a collective of kiddies hackers have a chance against the illuminati? Why is Picus almost the only media in the whole world?
The focus on augs is also very annoying. We're just awashed with it the whole time. You talk to someone: 98% it will be "augs are good" or "augs are bad". You read newspapers: augs. Etc. It's a Deus Ex game, there should be more importance given to anticipation.
Despite all of this, I consider this game as a true Deus Ex game. The universe MIGHT be less deep, but I find the rest far better than in HR and in GOTY.

Deus Ex: Mankind Divided is the follow-up for the critically acclaimed title Deus Ex: Human Revolution. It is an Actiongame with RPG and Stealth Elements, like the game before. In the following review I'll explain why I'm recommending it:
+ It is arguably as good than its precursor, offering you more Augmentations (basically your skills you can earn via leveling up), better graphics and a probably as good story and well written characters.
+ The main story is already pretty good (with a sadly big weakness I'll get to later), but you're also getting a lot of pretty good sidemissons, which are written pretty good aswell. Also the outcome of the story (like in the first one) is influenced by your ingame choices, making it exciting to play through again.
+ You're pretty free to play the game the way you want. You can play through the game without anybody noticing you or without killing anybody. Or, if you want, you can play this game as a total shooter and shoot your way through everybody, which actually should be fun with the new augmentations you'll get.
+ Graphics look really good and nice! Requires a good computer to work well.
+ Setting is great. This time you're in Prague most of the time, and the city is designed very well and fleshed out.
+ Again, great Soundtrack and Sounddesign. Fits the atmosphere so well and is just overall produced pretty well.
+ Lots of achievements, story related items and lots of cool stuff to discover.
- it doesn't feel that well optimized in terms of performance compared to other games. I had some glitches (maybe due to my old CPU) and a few crashes, but with a good enough computer you should be fine. Although it worked better on my laptop than on my older desktop.
- the story ends kind of abrupt and is overall shorter than the one in Human Revolution. When you're reaching the end of the game, it feels like there should be a last part, where you are able to resolve everything, but it goes to the credits.
Mabye they will add it as DLC, but in my opinion it should already be in the game. Still, the most part of the story arc is there.
:
An awesome game. It offers everything you'd want from a new Deus Ex, although the developers kind of left out the real end to the main story, which probably gets out as DLC (which sadly is the way to go in gaming industry).
Kind of performance heavy, so check if your pc is able to run this one!
One last thing: I'm kinda getting why people, who bought it for the full price as a pre-order or so, we're unsatisfied with it, but i refuse to go into the circle-jerk of bad reviews for this game.
I had a blast and enjoyed it and it is a really, really good game in my opinion.
That being said, I got this game for 20€ or so and it was more than worth it.
Arguably it may be even worth the full price.
EDIT:
In hindsight, I'll give it a bit lower rating, it honestly was somekind of a knee-jerk reaction to all the bad ratings. Still a great game imo. Also it seems like the ending will never come out, as DEUS EX seems to be on hold. Gives me another reason to downrate it.

This review is based on about 50 hrs play (of which maybe 10 away from screen), single player mode
In short you control a space ship, build a fleet of battle and support ships to accompany you, build a base and extend it, manage resources such as population, energy, credits and 6 material resources. Expand your territory with military bases and vanquish your neighbours. You win either by Economic, military or diplomatic achievements. The focus is on strategy rather than piloting/shooting skills of the ship you control.
I started a game on very easy, which I found was great to learn the game as there is no real tutorial. There is a very short first time tutorial once you make a profile, that explains how to control your spacecraft but it is rather simple (right mouse click to turn, space to stop/start engines). The early game time is spend on doing missions and flying around with your spacecraft, building up your base and buying and upgrading new buildings that will unlock more spacecrafts, weapons and technologies. This early phase of the game is fun but quickly becomes boring after a while as there is not much variation on the missions to do. However you only need to do it once and just look at it as a tutorial for the game.
One of the great things about this game is that when you start a new map (or game) everything you already unlocked and upgraded on your ship is ported to the new game (even the credits), so there is no need to repeat the early phase of the game with each map or start of a new game. Think of Terraria where you take your toon to different worlds but the level and inventory of the toon is saved. Of course in every new game you will have to build up your base from scratch.
The game or star system is made up of a hexagonal map where each hexagon is a sector. You can travel your ship from sector to sector by jumping, each sector can hold 1 building. Some sectors cannot support buildings (nebulas); sectors with resources can only hold mines, otherwise you can build a radio station (for more income) or military bases (strategic). But your first building will be your city or home base, choose carefully the sector to start from as to close to others will generate hostility but resources are important. There are 6 material resources on the map, but Titanium is the most important as it is used for every building. Your fleet only requires credits and no material, but material is need to upgrade and build buildings.
Strategy is around building military bases and fleets to protect your territory or attack enemies within range of the military bases. Each military base controls an area, at level 1 it will control each sector adjacent to the base, at level 2 it will control an area in a 2 sector range and at level 3 an area in a 3 sector range. You don’t directly control the fleets garrisoned in the military bases, but they will defend any installations that are attacked within its range and in war mode they will attack and destroy enemy installations (however not enemy control centers). Similarly each control center will control an area within 1 to 4 sectors depending on its level.
The first player who controls a sector will own the sector, the only way to conquer the sector is by destroying the base that controls the sector and any buildings in the sector that may exist.
By building hangars in your home base you can increase your fleet size and buy more ships to help you as you fly around and do missions or attack enemy sectors.
So once you have your base going and you have secured resources, it all comes down to building and upgrading military bases, buying fleets and doing missions to give you income bonus or improve relationship with neighbours.

Long I hesitated to buy this ugly looking game. Then I did and discovered a nice concept mixing several genres as space shooter, RTS, 4X and city building (which occur to be amongst my top favorite genres). Although as it was to be expected it lacks depth in both departments, lacking variety in weaponry and upgrades for the space shooter part, lacking the ship design part of the 4X, lacking tactical options for the RTS part to name but a few fields where a bit of depth could have made this title a milestone in gaming experiences.
But. Yet there is a but. It's dead on fun. The very simple game mechanics are intuitive in every sector and the alchemy between all the genres works just fine, as at the end while nothing is outstanding individually in this game, everything as a whole is decently clear and pleasantly easy to grasp. There are very few flaws and bugs and it runs smoothly even in the end game with huge fleets (the only thing I found "annoying" was the scavenging quest where some ships carcasses often overlap each others making it near to impossible sometimes to reap all of the materials, although that is very minor inconvenience indeed).
The game makes sure there is always something to do, and although it is grindy the fact you can setup mining stations and radars (economy stations actually) to get an income over time actually makes the questing minigames feel like a nice bonus instead of a repetitive chore. Now of course, the "distress call" and "pirate" quests are the most rewarding as they both provide credits and materials, with the former also providing a significant , temporary and cumulative increase to your income over time and you will most likely prioritze them over comets, battles and generally scavenging (with the exception of pirates and ship derelicts, sadly the other quests' difficulty and rewards do not increase with your progress).
An interesting feature of Beyond Sol is the profile-map dichotomy which allows you to save some technological progress (in the form of ship unlocks and upgrades as well as modules and weapons unlocks and upgrades) for when you start another map. You can also transfer a complete fleet with you from map to map, although it may be wise to have the economy to be able to sustain it (or sell the fleet for extra cash).
Beyond Sol is not a great game, although it is a great concept and it achieves, through its simplicity to be what a game should be, fun (of course provided you like at least a few genres which Beyond Sol mixes). I personnally would have added depth to it, not actual complexity just depth, but maybe there will be a Beyond Sol 2 in the future which may also look less ugly and uneven graphically which may actually do just that by digging deeper into the usual features found in the source genre it took inspiration from.
In the meantime, I recommend this relaxing game, if gameplay matters more to you than looks. Note its replayability is mainly based on how challenging you setup your game (map settings and AI difficulty) and on your profile progression.

Well, I feel its time to give this game a fair summary. Lord of the Rings Online is true to the T to Tolkiens Trilogy: The Lord of the Rings. Bare in minds this means a lot of differences if you expect there to be assimilations to the movies. That being said the books h definately delved deeper into the lore and ideas that Tolkien wanted to explore when creating the world of Arda.
Lord of the Rings Online is now a little over 9 years old as of the creation of this review and is sadly speculated to be taken down in the coming  years due to lack of funding and rights to the ownership through warner brothers. Many many players have come in and out of this game over the years to experience myriad updates and journeys. I myself started my journey into LotRO 3 years prior to now. And I found what the definition of an MMO truely is.
I have witnessed but a third of LotRO's life span but in that time have finished the story up to update 18 with my hunter reached the half way mark in leveling with a Rune-Keeper and had fun exploring and challenging other classes along with friends to the rough mark of level 20. With this I can tell you LotRO is a wonderful game.
LotRO provides and caters to all types of players. Hardcore MMO players can bash out levels swiftly find tough solo and multiplayer challenges at end game and the casual gamer who is in here for the experience can still sink many hours enjoying the combat and content the game has to offer.
Craft: Choose a proffession with 3 crafting skills within allowing you to create gear for yourself and harvest materials for friend that have different skills you can cater for. Hunt for materials, gather and make. Its simple and rewarding.
RolePlay:
LotRO allows players the freedom of doing what an MMO was designed for and it hits the mark harder than any other game, as a hunter I can make a campfire just out the town of Bree, smoke some pipe-weed, much on Lembas bread and listen to my kin play their music. By this I mean you can litterally do player made music and it is wonderful. People will spare time to listen to and you feel like a star when it happens.
Fight:
When you start the game you have the option for quite a few classes such as Guardian, Minstrel & Lore-Master. Each inspired by characters from Tolkien's Lord of the Rings. They each give you a unique play style and can be customised down trait trees to a specific deriverative of the class. Build yourself to play alone or to fight aloneside friends almost all classes can be brought to many different styles of combat and it does not get dull. The combat will set you up with a few working combo's but nothing really true, it leaves it up to you to fight the way you want and build abilities how you like. The combat itself feels smooth and satisfying, sound effects are on point and really feel good. Animations may be a bit dated but they still work well and feel fairly suited. You cans tart fighting weak enemies in your starting region. Move on to groups of mobs and eventually come to fight some that learn to buff themselves or gather squads to group up and take you down. The enemies change themselves up as you play through the game and it feels good learn to take your new opponents down. Or to crush them beneathe your heel when you have out leveled them.
UI:
The HUD and UI of LotRO has to be hands down the most customisable interace I have used in gaming... ever. absolutely everything can be moved and scaled EVERYTHING and it isn't difficult to do either.
Audio:
The audio is astounding rarely do you get a game that really slots the soundtrack perfectly into place but by the Gods if anything will be remembered about this game for year to come it will be the music. No you will not here the iconic shire theme or theme of the fellowship but they are replaced with equally memorable unique and above all amazing soundtracks. If you don't believe me wait until you enter Bree and tell me you can forget that wonderful rythm.
Atmosphere:
Now LotRO isn't exactly new and some fault it immediately for lack of texture quality or too little amount of polygons simply to forget the appeal of video game graphics when they are OPEN WORLD. This might be hard to get by at first but you can quickly come to appriciate how wonderful Middle-Earth actually looks. The design is for the big picture, zoom out your camera run into the distance the world is created picture perfect plains are open, hills steep ruins are run down and towns are bustling its all how it is meant to be in an RPG and mostly it feels like THE LORD OF THE RINGS.
Gameplay:
LotRO gives you a few things to do in the gameplay area. Quests the main scenario will take you through your own story as the saviour of Western Middle-Earth; Eriador and your fight against the shadows of Angmar. Later scenarios take you on the story to follow the Fellowship and fight for your life along side Rohan and Gondor. Side quests offer real rewards that are worth your time. Neatly set up so nearby quest objectives are as they should be, close to each other for convinience and a lot of enjoyment when handing them in by bulk. There is other stuff available to you as well such as deeds and skirmishes. Thse are the staples that make LotRO LotRO. Now most MMOs have their conventional dungeons but Lord of the Rings Online changed things up a bit with small enemies engagements similar to that of a dungeon. You may sometimes be running into a camp blind to wipe it of enemies take position fight counter attacks and be rewarded with loot but you might sometimes be defending and have some groups of goblins or tough Lietenants of the enemy pushing your ground for control. These are great fun to do with your friends on and can be done at all levels and for good rewards at that. Deeds are the second staple. Deeds allow you to go out into the world fulfill your duty as a hero and explore. Some are tough but they can be worth your time if you put that time into them. Deeds ask you to do a set number of tasks in each region of the world such as kill so many enemies, find certain objects, explore different places and help people out (quests). Each deed rewards you with Turbine points [which I will get to in the next section] & hard deeds will give you virtues which can be put towards buffing your character. Some give you marks a currency for trading to buy new gear and crafting recipes. Some give you loot-boxes you can open for free stuff. It ends up being worth it and seeing you have completed deeds in your log for an area is one of the most satisfying things in gaming I have experienced yet.

So after 500 hours I guess its time to write a review.
No matter which game I play, I always seem to come back to Lotro. It has its flaws, but yet there is just something special about it. The community in general are always helpful and willing to help out new players, and after the server migrations the world feels much more populated. Even if you are not a fan of J.R.R Tolkien's work, I would still recommend you try this game for at least the first 30 levels, as you would not have to buy a single thing until then.
Pros:
- Great Community
- The only game that allows you to explore most of Middle-Earth
- Very active RP groups if you are interested in that
- Hundreds of hours of content
- Possible to play this game completely free (You can earn Turbine points by doing deeds in-game)
- PvP is fun, as you can play either as the Free Peoples, or as Sauron's Army
Cons:
- The game is old, so even though it still looks very good, the outdated graphics might put some people off
- There is a lot that you would need to purchase or grind for, if you do not pay a monthly sub.
- Server issues can cause lag quite a lot, especially in PvP, though in general it is fine
- Balance issues with some classes, though the game is still being actively developed and balanced
So overall, I would score Lotro a 8/10, and would recommend anyone looking for a decent MMO or just a fun game to try it out.
Edit: 1300 hours and review still stands, loving it so far!

This game seems simple and casual upon first inspection but underneath this colorful facade you will discover a dark and twisted world like no other. Corporations experimenting on babies fire their assistant who curiously ruins an experiment simply by picking up the baby and in his confused misery following termination he seeks advice from a local surly waitress named "Flo." Wilson, the assistant in question, goes on to start his own daycare in his sister's basement which develops a massive following in a matter of days. He eventually is in charge of caring for hundreds of babies a day with the help of his robots who  don't perform their primary and only duties all that well. WIlson also has a strange habit of throwing away all his money and extra equipment that cost him thousands of dollars as well as downgrading all his machines the second he moves into a bigger working space. The fact that this clearly insane man who is borderline sexually obsessed with machines can have so much responsibility leads to questions regarding what kind of world these people live in. Where you pay upwards of $2000 to have a "friendly smile" which magically encourages people to give you more money. There's also the fact that fully clothed toddlers are thrown in with the other babies that causes some bewilderment. Welcome to the dark world of Diaper Dash. I sincerely hope this wins Game of the Year because it has one of the most unique and intriguing storylines I have seen in 2010. I highly recommend this addicting game.

After playing the first Scribblenauts game, I went into this with high hopes. Hopes that the game really didn't live up to. The levels are a pain to get around in, and some of them outright require flying, which is just annoying to have to reenable over and over again. The puzzles themselves really just seems overly repetitive, and it didn't feel like there was as much creativity involved in them.
In the first, areas could be cleared, whereas here there's a boss fight (these were rarely terribly interesting) but every time you visit a level it will be filled with a new set of randomly selected puzzles. It meant that I didn't really feel like it had the neat theming that was present in the first game. It also meant that having to clear out these smaller puzzles just felt repetitive and uninteresting.
Finally, the superhero element, while neat in some situations, largely just meant that there was a whole bunch of repetitively high powered foes and at a certain point, it just became frustating enough that my solution to every indication of violence was "Green lantern corps", which would bring in like 10 heroes at once. At least that made the achievement for 150 green lantern members happen faster.
The game should feel fun, and it just really, didn't.

This, IMHO is a very "meh" game.  There isn't really anything wrong with it, but there isn't really anyting right about it.  The game-play is not compelling at all.  I just mostly run around salvaging ships or mining comets, waiting for enough minerals to get the next city upgrade and that about sums up several hours of game-play.
Sure you can fight things, but for that, you need a fleet and to do that, you need a somewhat upgraded city.  Even then, combat isn't very intresting.  You just fly around mashing attacks as they come off cool-down, while your AI buddies do whatever it is they do.  Eventually one side or the other will win and that is the way all combats go.
The economy is also borked.  You build mining stations which will give you a steady stream of minerals, sometimes 2 streams.   There are two problems here.  Lets say that BLUE mineral is needed to build most things and then everything else needs BLUE + some other color.   You always end up waiting because you never have enough BLUE mineral.
This leads to the other problem, is that all your other mining stations keep cranking out minerals you do not need.  So what do you do?  You sell them, which is fine at first, but then you notice the prices get lower and lower.  Eventually every mineral but BLUE will be worthless.
Anway, there is also not much pressure to do anything, and  its just play at your own pace.  Mostly, you just do repetitive tasks which are not all that intresting.
The game is a nice idea, but its really after a short while.

I'm mostly giving this my thumbs up because I'm a sucker for "builder" games. It has about as much depth as a cheap board game though. This game would be 100x better had they thrown in some storylines, characters, or even a quest or two. Something to give some variety. There's also some weirdness with the GUI choices. Having said that, overall I enjoy it and find it satisfying in bursts.
Pros:
- Nice clean graphics
- Simple combat that is engaging but not twitch-happy
- Base, fleet, and ship building. Create your own empire and watch it grow
- Multiple viable paths to victory if you want to be bloodthirsty or popular or rich (should probably scale with the map better though)
Cons:
- Shallow gameplay. Do a half dozen activities a half million times.
- No storyline other than the intro video. Nothing has real context or reason. I felt I was wandering aimlessly a lot.
- UI weirdness (see below)
Suggestions:
- When managing fleets, put it in the same UI as purchasing fleets. That would've made sense. Instead I had to look up that the Fleet Management was in the corner of the map.
- When on the map, display current statistics (cargo, money, etc). I found myself toggling back and forth a lot.
- Display a timer for all events. I forget when they appeared and often reached an event only to see it expire.
- Allow zooming on the map. Zooming in 3rd person would also be welcome (just use fog of war if there are balance concerns).
- Add a ledger or commodities exchange or notes so that I can keep track of how much I paid for something when I go to sell it. Or track where I saw high or low prices. Any merchant worth their salt would do this. The game should be your accountant and help you make money.
- Just in general I found myself opening and closing windows to look behind or around them too much. It felt like the UI was tripping over itself and didn't have a good flow to it. The information is mostly there, it's just clunky.
- Add shortcut keys to all functions. Mostly the pause function needs a shortcut key, but add the others too.
- The hit box for selecting things with the mouse should be at least as big as the graphic, probably bigger. It's a bit frustrating to select anything. It's nearly impossible while in motion.

Ziggurat, developed by Milkstone Studios, puts you in the shoes of a magic user trying to prove their worth. They will have to do this by taking on a tower that is ever changing. No two games will be the same. Well there is a start and a finish to the tower, of course, but the configuration of the rooms, the enemies you will face, the upgrades you will come across, all of these will be random. You see this is a rogue-like, First Person Casting, fast-paced, dungeon crawler (well actually tower crawler as you will be ascending, not descending). You will have to be fast because if you hesitate, or take too long to act you will be killed in a heartbeat. I say this having died WAY TOO many times to start off.
Graphically this is a game that you really don't get to admire much of when enemies are involved. I will say this though, I love the fact that there is destructible objects in the game where you can blow off a little bit of steam, and if you are really luck perhaps you will find something hidden. There are several different types of rooms that you will have to familiarize yourself to. There is the guardian room (basically the room you will HAVE TO GO THROUGH to get to the next level), the guardian's key room (this is the room you will have to find in order to unlock the guardian that must be defeated to advance in the game), the trap room (this is where you are probably going to spend a lot of time cursing when you need precision and you end up just falling off the platform), the minion rooms (these come in all shape and sizes, basically this is where you will have to kill all the enemies to unlock the doors), the treasure room (a room that can give you a different spell to use, or perhaps something else to help you survive), and to mention one more room you have the, what I like to call, the sacrifice room (this is the room that you can give up some of your magic, nothing, or life to obtain something that might help you out further down the line.
Speaking of magic there is quite a variety of magical attacks that you will get to use. Some of them will simply come out of your wand, while others will be in the form of a magically loaded gun or bomb. The thing is that you will have your purple shooting wand (which is your basic attack) at your disposal at almost all times, the magic points needed to use this will regenerate over time. The other three types of spells, blue, green, and orange, have to be collected from defeating foes, and those spells of course can cause MUCH MORE damage than the purple.
To truly survive this game you are going to have to choose your level ups wisely. Once you have gained enough experience you will be given a choice of cards, each card has its own effect, and it will change the game for you. I HIGHLY recommend that you go the route I usually go, and that's the one where if there's a card that allows you to get more out of experience point pick ups. Did I miss out on some of the level ups, absolutely, but I was always leveling up, quickly, I might add, and that allowed me to really pump up my character. I thought that I might have safely made myself over-powered, but the final boss still crushed me like a little bug.
The enemies in the game all have a very unique look to them, there are bald chickens mixed with lizard looking creatures, there are blobs, there are elementals, there are screaming banshees, there are flying skulls, crab handed demons, and so much more. I really did enjoy the variety of enemies. Well at least the look of them, there were definitely some of them that I really didn't want to see as they seemed to be the ones that chased me right into the grave, over and over again.
To play this game you have the options of keyboard, or gamepad. I am here to tell you that the gamepad is the ONLY way to play this game. Try as I might with the keyboard and mouse, I was just never fast enough to last very long, but on my first gamepad playthrough, I actually got through the first level of the tower. The game is just so fast, at points, that I couldn't keep up with the pace, especially when it comes to changing spells out so that you can try to do as much damage as possible, and not be left vulnerable.
So the interesting thing about this game is that no matter how many times you play it, there's always going to be some new wrinkle, or design that is going to keep you on your toes. There's also other heroes that you will unlock as you play the game more and more, so in a way, even when you succeed you will still need to grind if you are going to be able to unlock the whole game.
I guess I should probably wrap up this review at this point. I will tell you this, at first I was ready to rage quit, and never come back to this game again, but once I found the comfort in playing with the gamepad, I definitely started to enjoy this game. Sure there were some difficult times, and some SERIOUSLY close calls (I beat a boss with basically 2 health left, if my spell hadn't killed him he would have killed me). So if you are looking for a fast paced first person shooter (magic casting) game where the levels will never truly be the same, you are going to have to get this game. If you are looking for something that is quick to pick up, this will not be the game for you. This is the kind of game that you have to initially play over and over again so that you can get a feel for it, and then find the best way to survive. This will definitely cut away at potential gamers, but those who are willing to stick it out are definitely going to find a game where you are going to lose track of time, and hopefully find victory. This game gets an 8.2 out of 10.

RECYCLE, once I got it working, turned out to be a fairly competent simulator.  It doesn't win any awards in the physics department (you bounce off objects, drive through people, etc.), but it is fairly good at being a garbage sim.  You're forced to be in control of a vehicle but can set the others on autopilot should you have more than one.  If you're not in the mood to drive at all, you can assign your other trucks to their usual routes and when they return, send them right back out again to the ones you'd normally do (Your day ends at 4 PM, so try to make sure you have enough trucks to handle the extra loads).  You gain XP and money either way you do it, so you can sit back and manage or take the reigns yourself...though I have to admit the AI is MUCH faster at doing the job.  Vehicles and other features unlock as you play, though you don't actually create routes...you purchase pre-planned ones and send your trucks out accordingly.  You CAN however assign the days the routes get services.
Verdict: I myself wouldn't pay $24.99 for this game, though I WOULD grab it during a sale.
Fixing the crash on startup error can be done as follows:
1) Open your Steam/Steam Apps/Common/RECYCLE/System folder and COPY the 7 ICOM files to...
2) Open your C Drive/Users/Your Name/Documents/My Games/ Recycle/System.  Simply overwrite the 3 existing ICOM files.

It's an ok game, but after playing this i know i don't want to play any of the other Far Cries (and i haven't). It is bland and repetitive. Story missions and the theme is ok, but nothing really engaging, spectacular, at times stupid even. I get that this was an intention to beat on trash movies cliches, but it was too much some times. Outside of the main story it is an open world which is pretty empty. Yeah with some fights between scientists and commandos going on here and there. It was fun to roam in a jeep, but not for long. Side quest are all similar (go and kill someone and maybe save some scientist jerk). I hated missions requiring you to do stealth in an open field surrounded by 20+ enemies. "Cutscenes" were often too long and, i don't know, i just didn't liked how they sounded and looked. I didn't get the leveling thing as you couldn't choose a skill, it was just a linear progression which happened automatically. I hated some animations like pilfering cyberhearts (which you needed sometimes to distract dragons) or shotgun reloading cycle which took to long to start shooting again.
Then the general design. Saves somethimes weren't working. So i ended up only using checkpoints. And once i had to listen to some story dialog like 10 times while dying on some side quest and loading again. Stupid system of repeating everything when you load a save. After a recent uPlay update it started to mess with Blood Dragon launch and jumped in front of it making BD starting in a windowed state, so i had to restart it every time (that' because uPlay wasn't already running, yeah, i don't want some program to run all the time when i only need it for one game occasionally). That's another point why i won't play Far Cry or other Ubisoft game.
All in all, it was fun to shoot enemies and ride the jeep at times, but it was also a bland, sometimes boring game with an overdone humour. Can't call it a good game.
